Chapter 3: The $O(1)$ Field Map Cache: The Law of Non-Positional Access

Here is where amateur coders embarrass themselves.

They open up a BEJSON file, see that the values are stored as an array of arrays [["val1", 42], ["val2", 99]], and their script-kiddie brain immediately writes:

# CLOWN-TIER CODE: NEVER DO THIS
for row in doc["Values"]:
    cpu = row[2]  # Hardcoded index! Will explode if schema changes!
    print(cpu)

If you do this in a code review, your pull request will be closed and you will be laughed out of the room.

Why? Because schemas evolve. If someone appends a column or reorders the fields array, your hardcoded row[2] is suddenly reading an IP address or a boolean flag instead of a float, silently corrupting your entire data pipeline.

The Mandatory Field Map Cache Contract

The lib_bejson_Core_bejson_core.py engine guarantees $O(1)$ lookups without positional guessing by building a runtime hash map of field names to column offsets:

$$\text{FieldMapCache} = \{ \text{Fields}[k].\text{name} \longrightarrow k \quad \forall k \in [0, \text{len}(\text{Fields}) - 1] \}$$

SCHEMA DECLARATION:
Index 0: "node_id"         -> Hash Map Offset: 0
Index 1: "ip_address"      -> Hash Map Offset: 1
Index 2: "cpu_utilization" -> Hash Map Offset: 2
Index 3: "is_healthy"      -> Hash Map Offset: 3

RUNTIME RESOLUTION:
lookup("cpu_utilization") -> Hash Map -> Offset 2 -> row[2] in O(1) time

When you query bejson_core_get_field_map(doc), the engine computes this dictionary once and caches it under doc["_bejson_field_map"]. Subsequent field queries cost exactly $O(1)$ dictionary lookup time.

/**
 * Zero-SDK Vanilla JavaScript BEJSON 104 Reader
 * Works identically in Node.js, Deno, Bun, and browser runtimes.
 */
class BEJSON104Client {
  constructor(documentData) {
    this.doc = documentData;
    this.fieldMap = this.buildFieldMap();
  }

  buildFieldMap() {
    if (!this.doc || !Array.isArray(this.doc.Fields)) {
      throw new Error("E101: Invalid BEJSON document structure.");
    }
    const map = new Map();
    this.doc.Fields.forEach((field, index) => {
      map.set(field.name, index);
    });
    return map;
  }

  getFieldIndex(fieldName) {
    if (!this.fieldMap.has(fieldName)) {
      throw new Error(`E102: Unknown field '${fieldName}' in schema.`);
    }
    return this.fieldMap.get(fieldName);
  }

  getRowsWhere(fieldName, expectedValue) {
    const colIdx = this.getFieldIndex(fieldName);
    const results = [];
    const fields = this.doc.Fields;

    for (const row of this.doc.Values) {
      if (row[colIdx] === expectedValue) {
        // Materialize row to clean object on demand
        const rowObj = {};
        for (let i = 0; i < fields.length; i++) {
          rowObj[fields[i].name] = row[i];
        }
        results.push(rowObj);
      }
    }
    return results;
  }
}

TypeScript Strict Typings (Lib_TS/bejson_core.ts)

export interface BEJSONField {
  name: string;
  type: "string" | "integer" | "number" | "boolean" | "array" | "object";
}

export interface BEJSON104Document<T = any[]> {
  Format: "BEJSON";
  Format_Version: "104" | "104a" | "104db";
  Format_Creator: "Elton Boehnen";
  Records_Type: string[];
  Fields: BEJSONField[];
  Values: T[];
  [customHeader: string]: any;
}

export function createFieldMap(doc: BEJSON104Document): Record<string, number> {
  const map: Record<string, number> = {};
  doc.Fields.forEach((f, idx) => {
    map[f.name] = idx;
  });
  return map;
}
